reasons: The cited § 14.10 binds only Customer: Customer needs IBM's consent (with a narrow merger/consolidation/acquisition carve-out) while IBM's assignment is entirely unrestricted — no consent standard and no competitor bar. That asymmetry fails the fallback, which contemplates a mutual right to assign to successors and a reasonable-consent standard for other assignments, so the deviation classification is correct rather than over-flagging an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a targeted edit: it keeps the original consent sentence, voiding sentence and continuing-liability sentence intact, widens the Customer carve-out to affiliates and sale of substantially all assets, and adds one sentence subjecting IBM's assignment to Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld) with a competitor bar. The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.656) reflects the added mutuality sentence, which the rule expressly requires ('Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer'); no unnecessary text was disturbed.

Direction is correct and pro-Customer; nothing in the edit worsens our position, and the redline is legally coherent (the existing 'void' and 'Customer will remain liable' language still reads sensibly).

The comment is accurate, in the required first-person plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix, explains both changes and offers the fallback; the rationale correctly notes the absence of any change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no walk-away issue is overstated, and § 14.8 subcontracting is left alone (no double-flagging).
